name: Demo Corp (fictional)

sources.label: Fictional demo data: option prices from a Heston model (v0 0.05, kappa 1.8, theta 0.06, xi 0.7, rho -0.65)

insights: The market is open (10:30 New York). The stock price is current; option quotes are delayed by about 15 minutes.

30-day implied volatility is 21,8 % against 21,5 % realised over the last 21 trading days: options price similar moves than the recent past (gap 0,3 pts). The gap is usually positive (the volatility risk premium).

Skew: the 25-delta put trades at 23,9 % volatility, 6,2 pts above the 25-delta call (17,6 %); the market pays more for protection against a fall than for upside. Constant-volatility Black–Scholes cannot show this.
The term structure is inverted (stress in the near term): 22,2 % at 7 days, 20,5 % at 399 days.

Selected 103 put (2027-12-17, 399,2 days): market mid 8,31 $, implied volatility 20,6 %. One at-the-money volatility (20,5 %) would give 8,29 $ in Black–Scholes; the 0,03 $ gap comes from the smile, not from an opportunity.

Nowcast: when the quotes were made the stock was about 99,61 $; it is now 100,00 $. At the same implied volatility, Black–Scholes carries that move to about 8,14 $ for the selected option (−0,18 $); the delayed quote may not include the move yet. A model estimate.
The early-exercise right is worth 0,45 $ (American minus European, binomial tree).
Risk-neutral chance of finishing in the money: 43,9% (corrected for the smile's slope; one-volatility N(d₂) would say 53,8%). A pricing quantity, not a real-world forecast.
The at-the-money straddle (103) costs 16,9% of the price: the market prices a move of about ±16,9% to expiry (size, not direction).
